data.body_html:
Planning a marbella yacht charter august 2039 means booking early, knowing the weather, and picking the right boat. August is peak season on the Costa del Sol: sea temperatures hit 24°C, days are long, and the coast buzzes with energy. But with crowds come challenges – calm morning seas can turn to afternoon breezes, and popular anchorages fill fast. This guide covers everything you need: typical conditions, best anchorages, which yacht suits your group, and insider tips to make your day on the water seamless. All our charters depart from Puerto Banús, include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance. No hidden costs.

August Weather and Sea Conditions

August in Marbella delivers consistent sunshine and high temperatures averaging 30–34°C. Sea surface temperatures hover around 24°C, ideal for swimming and water sports. Prevailing winds are light westerlies at 5–12 knots, with the sea state typically calm (sea state 1–2) in the morning. By mid-afternoon, a light thermal breeze may pick up, but swells rarely exceed 0.5m. Visibility is excellent – often 20+ nautical miles. For the best conditions, plan to depart by 10:00 and return by 18:00. This avoids the strongest sun and any late-afternoon chop.

Best Anchorages and Routes for August

From Puerto Banús, you have several outstanding options. Head west to Cala del Faro – a sheltered cove with clear water, about 20 minutes from port. Further west, Estepona offers a long sandy beach and calm anchorage. Eastbound, Cala Cortés near Cabopino is a favourite for its turquoise water and rocky cliffs. For a livelier scene, anchor off the Golden Mile or right in front of Puerto Banús – but expect more boats. If you want a longer cruise, set course for Sotogrande (about 1.5 hours at 20 knots) for a chic marina lunch. All routes offer stunning views of La Concha mountain.

Choosing the Right Yacht for Your Group

Your group size and budget determine the best fit. For up to 9 guests, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (both Tier A) are excellent value at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full day (8 hours). For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) includes a free jet ski and starts at €4,719 for 4 hours. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers ample deck space and a flybridge for sunbathing. If you prefer a sailing catamaran, the Lagoon 380 (11.6m, 10 pax) provides stability and a shallow draft for close-to-shore anchoring. For ultimate luxury, the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) is a statement vessel. All boats depart from Puerto Banús and include skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks.

Navigational Tips for Peak Season

  • Book early – August slots fill 4+ weeks ahead. Secure your preferred yacht now.
  • Anchor carefully – Popular coves get crowded. Use a bow anchor and stern line to shore where permitted. Our skippers know the best spots.
  • Watch for jet skis and paddleboarders – August sees heavy water traffic near beaches. Maintain a safe speed and keep a lookout.
  • Plan for afternoon breeze – While light, it can create a gentle chop returning to port. Nothing to worry about, but worth noting for comfort.
  • Hydrate and protect – Bring plenty of water (we provide soft drinks and water) and high-SPF sunscreen. The sun is intense.

What’s Included in Your Charter

Every charter with us includes: a licensed skipper (speaks English and Spanish), fuel for the day, bottled water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks (crisps, nuts, olives), full insurance, safety equipment (life jackets, flares, first aid), and Spanish IVA (21%). No extra charges. You can bring your own food or arrange catering – just let us know. The skipper will handle navigation, anchoring, and safety briefings. You just relax and enjoy.

Sample August Itinerary – Full Day (8 hours)

TimeActivity
10:00Board your yacht at Puerto Banús. Safety briefing and welcome drinks.
10:30Depart west towards Cala del Faro. Cruise past the Golden Mile.
11:15Anchor at Cala del Faro. Swim, snorkel, and enjoy snacks.
13:00Lunch on board (own arrangement or pre-ordered).
14:30Slow cruise east towards Cabopino. Spot dolphins often.
15:30Anchor at Cala Cortés. More swimming and jet ski (if on Mangusta 80).
17:00Return to Puerto Banús. Sunset views of La Concha.
18:00Disembark. Memories made.
